You could try to get him talking to you about the things he actually wants in life. If you can have some one on one time with him and just talk about what he wants to do in life, where he wants to be and try to get him to actually talk about his future with you, then it may open up his eyes a little bit as to what he's actually doing with his life. He sounds like the kind of guy that is just going to go with the flow and take the easiest route possible, and if you do that in life then you're going to have a pretty shitty life, which is obviously what is happening right now. Once you get him talking about where he wants to be and what he wants to do, you can get him to explore his options and help make suggestions for him moving forward. It's important to understand someone's mindset and understand why a person does things or feels the way they do, and it's important for the person to understand that as well. He's clearly unhappy from the way you describe things, but sometimes when you're in a shitty situation it doesn't feel like there is a way out, easy, hard or otherwise.

So yeah if I was in your shoes I'd have a chat with him about his goals and aspirations and if he doesn't have any then get him thinking about them. Goals are so important in life, without them you can lack direction and lose motivation, settling for less. As someone who was in a rut like this, it really helped me to have someone else question where I wanted to be and what I wanted to do. Once you figure that out then you can figure out how to get what you want and where you want.

I'm giving said advice from a counselling background as well, that's what I'm learning to be. It's important not to force him to do anything he doesn't want to do, but rather understand his point of view and respect it - once you do that and he sees that you respect his point of view, you can then challenge that point of view and maybe get him to realise that life could be better if he wanted it to be. :) Be honest but be compassionate, it's a fine line but I believe if you really care about him as a friend you will be able to get him to open up so you can be honest about how you feel about the situation as well, he'll be more willing to listen to what you have to say if you give him the time of day to say his piece as well. Hope that kind of makes sense, and hope this advice might help your friend.

Just keep in mind that you can't change a person, but you can help them to change themselves if they are willing to change for the better. You will figure it out very quickly if he is willing to make a change, or whether he does not care about himself. If you don't feel like you can help him in that way to sort his life out, you could always refer him to a counsellor who may be able to help guide him on a better path! Best of luck :)
